sample.n_note: n_paper (300 / 95 / 300) counts recruited HITs; Exp. 1 bot-check failures could never submit, so they are not among the 300. Agent sessions that fail the bot check end screened_out, so running n_paper exp1 sessions leaves fewer than 300 completers; top up sessions to reach 300 completed before applying the paper's exclusions

(arm == 'exp1' and sub('^\\s+|\\s+$', '', answer('e1_survey.language') or '') in ['United States']) or (arm == 'exp2a' and answer('a_survey.language') in ['hindi', 'female', 'russian']) or (arm == 'exp2b' and answer('b_survey.language') in ['Russian', 'Ukrainian', 'Arabic', 'chinese', 'hungarian', 'spanish']) or ((('uncoded' if not search('[a-z]', lower((answer('e1_survey.language') if arm == 'exp1' else (answer('a_survey.language') if arm == 'exp2a' else answer('b_survey.language'))) or '')) else ('english' if search('^(american |us |u[.]s[.] )?english[.!]?$', lower(normalize((answer('e1_survey.language') if arm == 'exp1' else (answer('a_survey.language') if arm == 'exp2a' else answer('b_survey.language')))))) else ('not_english' if search('^(spanish|french|german|chinese|mandarin|cantonese|hindi|tamil|telugu|portuguese|russian|italian|japanese|korean|vietnamese|tagalog|arabic|urdu|bengali|malayalam|polish|ukrainian)[.!]?$', lower(normalize((answer('e1_survey.language') if arm == 'exp1' else (answer('a_survey.language') if arm == 'exp2a' else answer('b_survey.language')))))) else 'needs_coder')))) == 'not_english') or (arm == 'exp1' and (not search('\\S', answer('e1_survey.language')) or sub('^\\s+|\\s+$', '', answer('e1_survey.language')) == 'NA')) or (arm == 'exp2a' and answer('a_survey.language') == 'NA') or (arm == 'exp2b' and answer('b_survey.language') in ['', None, 'NA'])
exclusions.pending_coding: needs_coder replies are KEPT in every effect until the coder step has run (not held out); their share is reported per run from session.native_language_code; after coding, 'not_english' ones are excluded, then the four 2-sd population cut-offs (which run after language_native, after_exclusions) are recomputed, then the effects

native_language.why: the authors' coding of the native-language box is not printed (supp. p. 2 gives only the criterion); this rule codes clear replies only: a bare English / American English -> english, a bare single other language -> not_english, empty or letterless -> uncoded, anything else (bilingual, typos, sentences) -> needs_coder for a declared coder applying the supplement's criterion. The exact strings the authors' R preprocessing excluded by hand (AUTH_LANG, source 'analysis') are arm-scoped, so they are not part of this text-only rule: exclusions.language_native and session.native_language_code apply each list in its own arm
native_language.apply: ('uncoded' if not search('[a-z]', lower(text or '')) else ('english' if search('^(american |us |u[.]s[.] )?english[.!]?$', lower(normalize(text))) else ('not_english' if search('^(spanish|french|german|chinese|mandarin|cantonese|hindi|tamil|telugu|portuguese|russian|italian|japanese|korean|vietnamese|tagalog|arabic|urdu|bengali|malayalam|polish|ukrainian)[.!]?$', lower(normalize(text))) else 'needs_coder')))

coder.input: the reply text and its experiment (exp1 / exp2a / exp2b; blind to condition and ratings)
coder.provenance: recorded per run; never mixed with rule codes

bot_check.why: not a coding of free text: the software's own exact check of the bot-check box (experiment.js botcaptcha: response.replace(' ', '') removes the first space only; compared case-insensitively with the listener's name); the flow applies the same expression with item = the drawn listener
bot_check.apply: 'correct' if lower(([(text or '')[:i] + (text or '')[i + 1:] for i in range(len((text or ''))) if (text or '')[i] == ' '] + [(text or '')])[0]) == lower(item) else 'incorrect'

analysis.targets_note: no cell values are printed: Figs. 2, 3, 5, 6, A2 are graphical only; the printed numbers are mixed-model coefficients, Spearman correlations and BIC/AIC

effects.label: Exp. 1 prior rating: higher- minus lower-probability fact (manipulation check)

compareAs.reason: dummy-coded fixed effect of fact type; every participant has 10 lower- and 10 higher-probability targets, so the coefficient is close to the mean within-participant difference (derived; random-slope weighting differs)

effects.label: Exp. 1 certainty rating: higher- minus lower-probability fact

compareAs.reason: dummy-coded fixed effect of fact type; every participant has 10 lower- and 10 higher-probability targets, so the coefficient is close to the mean within-participant difference (derived; random-slope weighting differs)

compareAs.reason: dummy-coded fixed effect of fact type; every participant has 10 lower- and 10 higher-probability targets, so the coefficient is close to the mean within-participant difference (derived; random-slope weighting differs)

effects.label: Exp. 1 certainty by the participant's own prior rating (target trials)
effects.scoring_why: the paper prints a mixed-model slope (beta 0.28); the engine computes Pearson r over trial rows (no clustering), so only the sign is comparable

unsupported.what: group-level prior predictor (Exp. 1 beta 0.31, Exp. 2b beta 0.34 from Exp. 2a item means)
unsupported.why: needs item means over the whole sample (Exp. 2b: over another arm) as a trial-level predictor

unsupported.what: Spearman r = .977 (Exp. 2a vs Exp. 1 item prior means), .986 / .988 / .991 with Tonhauser & Degen
unsupported.why: cross-arm item means; T&D is another sample
